content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm facing a new issue: my computer doesn't display the proper connection method and I'm unable to send the program. I recently upgraded to Windows 7 Professional. I've tried both WiFi and ethernet connections. I updated to [product_name] [version_no]. My [product_name] is accessible over the internet, and the modem ports are open. I can use the software via the server, and my PC recognizes the device. Thanks in advance for your help. [url]
It appears the network card for [product_name] wasn't set up correctly. What happens when you confirm the restart message for [product_name]?
I'm not sure why my computer sees the [product_name], but I can't interact with it. So unfortunately, I'm unable to proceed. [url]
All fields in the PC's network settings show 0.0.0.0. That's incorrect.
I can't input anything; [product_name] doesn't allow me to make changes. I suspect the issue lies with the PC.
The [product_name] itself seems fine.
How can I assist you? I keep asking questions but don't receive answers.
I've answered each time and shared a Dropbox link showing the issue. You've helped me before, but now I suspect the problem is with the PC. I'll check my computer.
I've asked you this twice: where is your response?

Sharing a Dropbox folder is helpful, but it might be better to switch [product_name] to English first. Have you tried clicking the blue refresh button in the transfer window? It searches for any [product_name] across subnets. Regards, [user_name]
I've addressed the main issue; is that correct? [url] I'm going to uninstall [product_name] and won't connect USB. I've asked you this twice: where is your response?
I've asked you this twice: where is your response?
Uninstall [product_name] and reinstall it. Make sure to launch setup as an administrator.
Thanks, [user_name]. I'll try this later and update you once I do.

I uninstalled and reinstalled [product_name], but the issue persists. One question: what should I do about the USB option if I'm only using WiFi or ethernet? I installed [product_name] first, then [product_name] [version_no]. [url] I've asked you this twice: where is your response?
Yes, my PC reads all the numbers related to the [product_name], including the MAC address.
The USB driver is only necessary for older [product_name] versions and original [company_name] USB cables. For newer [product_name] versions, it's not needed.
How are you connecting via Ethernet cable to the [product_name]? Is there a LAN card in your computer or are you connecting directly? Or are you using a WiFi card?
I tried connecting both ways—via home Ethernet and WiFi—just as I did before updating Windows on my laptop. I think my laptop's LAN card isn't being recognized.
That seems to be the case. I have a LAN card and [product_name] detects it, setting the IP and subnet mask automatically.
I'm unable to do this. Is it possible that I installed a demo version?
You're unsure if it's the demo or full version? With the demo, you can't connect to a [product_name]. Features like program transfer, online monitoring, reading firmware, etc., aren't available.
In this situation, it's not a demo version.
After performing a Windows update, everything is working fine now. Thanks anyway.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are having difficulties connecting [product_name] to a device after upgrading to Windows 7 Professional. Although the PC detects the device, necessary network fields display 0.0.0.0 and can't be edited, preventing connection setup. Users are frustrated by unclear error prompts in the software and uncertainty about whether the problem lies with the PC, network configuration, or the application itself.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to offer a clear and direct process for manual device connection and program transfer, regardless of operating system changes. There is also an expectation for explicit error messaging and the ability to resolve connection problems directly within the software.
